summary: Catherine Ludvik is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto by 2001 under David Waterhouse, Werner Knobl, Antonino Forte, and Yuko Matsuda, and held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Hanazono University.
Cathy Cantwell specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Kent (circa 1984–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oxford, Cambridge (under E. B. Cowell), and under Theodor Benfey. He worked at the British Museum, British Library, and as Professor of Sanskrit at UCL and Cambridge.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (circa 1937–1941). He held academic posts at Yale University (circa 1949–1951), the University of Chicago (circa 1967–1970), and the University of Virginia as Professor of English (circa 1970–1991).
Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Delog Dawa Drolma, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche (circa 1959–1987).

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul, who works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi. He served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. After earning a doctorate in philosophy from the University of Oxford, he held posts at Clare Hall, Cambridge, Trinity College, Oxford, the National University of Singapore, and Lancaster University.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. In 2012, he was attested as a professor at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.
Champa Thupten Zongtse is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who held posts at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1991 and as a lecturer in 2009.

Chandrabhal Tripathi was an Indologist who earned his PhD under Ernst Waldschmidt at the University of Göttingen (circa 1958–1962). He held posts at Göttingen, the University of Cologne, Free University of Berlin, and Humboldt University of Berlin.
Chang-geun Hwang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and earned his PhD from UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt and Noritoshi Aramaki, later serving as professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Chanju Mun is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under Charles Hallisey, Masahiro Shimoda, Morten Schlütter, Gudrun Bühnemann, and John D. Dunne.

Charlene Elizabeth Makley specializes in Tibetology and anthropology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999 under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport, and later became an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles A. Moore was a philosopher who studied at Yale University (circa 1922–1932). He served as a professor at the University of Hawaii (circa 1936–1967) and edited Philosophy East and West (circa 1951–1967).

Charles B. Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and held associate professorship and associate dean roles at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).

Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro (attested 1998–2006) and was a National Humanities Center Fellow (2009–2010).

Charles Duroiselle was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held positions at EFEO (circa 1903), the University of Yangon (circa 1905–1919), the Archaeological Survey of India (1919, 1936), and the Department of Archaeology, National Museum and National Library (1936).

Charles Edmund Godakumbura was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and archaeologist who studied at Kingswood College and served as a Senior Lecturer at the University of London (circa 1953–1958).

Charles Elliott was an Indologist who worked for the East India Company from circa 1795 to 1827 and served as treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1837 to 1856.
